decisions.statement: A message is a page under the message page type.
A message page's name opens with no digit.
A message is written to the page store alone.
A message page names its seat by page type and slug, and reads back as the name.
A message addressed to no seat the seat index knows is refused.
An unreadable seat index writes rather than refusing.
A message lands at the path the composer gives rather than at one worked out again here.
A message whose page would be over the byte ceiling is refused rather than landed.
A page over that ceiling is a page no later change can write.
A message is claimed and taken at the path the index files that message at.
A page composer may give a message a folder of its own, so the path is asked.
A message the index does not name is claimed and taken at the composed path.
A message is reached by the index rather than by listing one folder.
A message page the index files outside the one folder read here is left out.
Which store has a message is answered by the file on disk.
The shape of a message's id answers which store has the message never.
Reading a message is the message file's absence.
A claim on a message is a value beside the message rather than a change to the page.
The value beside a message is dropped for the store the message was found in.
The folder a watch is handed is the folder a message arrives in.
That folder is asked of the index rather than spelled here.
No folder a message page sits in is written in this code.

definition: a message on disk: written as a page, read from both stores, and taken once read
